conviction_note: Peer evidence since Nokia last spoke cuts both ways: Ericsson's 7% Q3 revenue beat (strong RAN in India and Japan) and Ciena's growing backlog and FY27 +30% point up. Ericsson's warning that component costs will weigh on 2027 gross margin, a comparable-EBIT consensus (EUR 453-462m) sitting above Nokia's own 'roughly flat' guide (~EUR 434m), and Nokia's warning that Q2's EUR 2.8bn AI and cloud orders will not repeat every quarter point down. Findings sum to -0.6 and p_up stays 50, so the scaled move is 0. The size of the move is 7.5%: an 8.3% implied move in a risk-off AI and optical tape, with the Q4 hockey stick and the 2027 margin commentary as the swing lines.
bar: Q3 net sales EUR 5,054m (Infront, 21 analysts, 15 Oct, via Inderes preview 19 Oct: https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/nokia-q326-preview-blikket-rettet-mod-ai-ordrer-og-vaekstforventninger-for-de-kommende-ar) and EUR 5,058m (FactSet, 23 estimates, Placera 19 Oct: https://www.placera.se/telegram/nokia-nokia-vantas-redovisa-462-miljoner-euro-i-justerat-rorelseresultat-factset-20261019); the two agree and sit at the midpoint of the company guide (Q3 +3-7% q-o-q on Q2's EUR 4,815m, i.e. EUR 4,959-5,152m; Q2 release https://www.inderes.fi/en/releases/nokia-corporation-report-for-q2-and-half-year-2026). Comparable operating profit: Infront EUR 453m (range 417-512) and FactSet EUR 462m, both ABOVE the company guide of 'roughly flat' on Q2's EUR 434m (Inderes estimate 435). Comparable EPS EUR 0.06. FY26 comparable operating profit guide EUR 2.1-2.6bn, 'somewhat above the midpoint'; consensus ~EUR 2.40bn, which implies a Q4 of about EUR 1.2bn.
positioning_check: Short interest 86.5M ADR shares at the 30 Sep 2026 settlement, up 55.8% from 55.5M, days to cover 1.00 on 90.6M average daily volume (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/nok/short-interest, read 2026-10-21). That is under 2% of shares and not crowded. 25-delta skew -4.86 vol points: calls are bid over puts ('upside paid'), and put/call OI is 0.54. ATM IV is 120.7% on the 23 Oct expiry, with an event-implied move of 8.3%. Tape: -13.2% over 20 days, -1.9% over 5, -45% from the 52-week high (a June peak), realised vol 50%. The drawdown runs alongside an AI and optical sector rotation (SOX -4.3% on 14 Oct after the Broadcom and Intel CEOs' AI-funding warnings; COHR, LITE and AAOI down 5-9% on 14-15 Oct).

findings.finding: Ericsson's Q3 (15 Oct, after Nokia last spoke on 23 Jul) printed net sales of SEK 59.5bn against an LSEG consensus of SEK 55.4bn (+7%), with organic growth of +7% and Networks sales +17% q-o-q on India and Japan. That is a direct read-through to Nokia Mobile Infrastructure (Q3 consensus ~EUR 2.8bn, +2% y-o-y; Inderes) and to the revenue line, where consensus sits only at the midpoint of Nokia's 3-7% q-o-q guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nokia's own prints (rebuilt, because the baseline's 8 'moves' are share-transfer 6-Ks, verified for 15 Oct and 8 Sep): Q2 on 23 Jul 2026 beat on comparable operating profit (EUR 434m) and fell about 5-7% on the soft Q3 guide (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/nokia-s-massive-ai-orders-overshadow-soft-guidance-bofa-sees-upside/cZZYLRvR7Uu). Q1 on 23 Apr missed revenue, raised the Network Infrastructure guide and rose about +6.5% (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/NOK/q1-2026/, approximate). This name trades on guidance and orders, not on reported-quarter revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Nokia's revenue consensus (EUR 5,054m on 15 Oct, 5,058m on 19 Oct) did not move after Ericsson's beat, and NOK fell in the week after Ericsson rose 9-12%. Had the read-through been priced, the consensus would sit in the upper half of the guide and NOK would have tracked ERIC. Jefferies framed Ericsson's strength as specific to Ericsson ('lack of AI exposure'), and part of Ericsson's Networks margin was retroactive IPR revenue, which limits the transfer to Nokia.
findings.independence: Ericsson's own release (https://www.ericsson.com/en/press-releases/2026/10/ericsson-reports-third-quarter-results-2026) and RTTNews (https://www.rttnews.com/3699316/ericsson-q3-profit-drops-sales-rise-simplifies-operating-structure-stock-gains.aspx) confirm the numbers; that is the same event, not an independent pointer to Nokia. It is a peer proxy: Nokia has not confirmed anything since 23 Jul.

findings.finding: Ciena (3 Sep, after Nokia's Q2) reported backlog of $8.5bn (+$0.8bn q-o-q), expected above $10bn by fiscal year end, said one month into FQ4 it had booked nearly as much as in all of FQ3, and guided FY27 revenue +30% or more. Inderes adds that Ciena is raising prices 10-20%. Nokia's own FY26 Optical+IP guide of 18-20% (Network Infrastructure 12-14%) looks conservative against that, which raises the odds of a Network Infrastructure guide raise or strong AI and cloud order commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Network Infrastructure guide raise at Q1 (23 Apr 2026) coincided with roughly +6.5% despite a revenue miss. At Q2 the guide was held (only technically raised) and the stock fell about 5-7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inderes's 19 Oct preview still carries Network Infrastructure at about +14% and Optical+IP at 19%, inside the existing guide, and FY consensus EBIT of EUR 2.40bn sits only slightly above the midpoint. Had a raise been expected, consensus would sit at or above the top of the range. The optical complex sold off 5-9% on 14-15 Oct on AI-funding fears, so the market is discounting optical demand rather than extrapolating Ciena.
findings.independence: Inderes preview (https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/nokia-q326-preview-blikket-rettet-mod-ai-ordrer-og-vaekstforventninger-for-de-kommende-ar) notes that Nokia's optical and IP targets look cautious against peers and cites Ciena's price increases. Also https://app.sentisense.ai/stories/ciena-posts-record-q3-revenue-on-ai-demand-as-stock-fluctuates-09032026 (Ciena fell 10% on an in-line guide, a reminder that the sector sells in-line numbers).

findings.finding: Component and memory cost inflation is a margin risk to the outlook. Ericsson's Q3 release (15 Oct) says 'component costs are a headwind to gross margin next year'. TrendForce puts CPU, DRAM and SSD at 68% of a benchmark notebook BOM in Q3 2026, against 45% in Q1 2025. Nokia already guided Mobile Infrastructure gross margin down to 44-46% in Q3 from 49% in Q2. If Nokia echoes Ericsson on 2027, or softens its 'meaningful' Q4 step-up (FY consensus needs about EUR 1.2bn in Q4), the outlook line takes it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (23 Jul 2026): a held FY guide plus a soft Q3 guide took the stock down about 5-7% despite a profit beat. Q4 2025 (Jan 2026): a cautious 2026 guide made the stock slip (https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/nokia-oyj-HEL:NOKIA/news/nokia-slips-as-cautious-2026-guidance-disappoints-019e6a08-038d-7e20-9861-50fa3e020c0a/).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Ericsson said it publicly and still rose 9%, and Inderes lists component availability and price increases as a watch item. What is not priced is a quantified Nokia number. FY consensus sits slightly above the guide midpoint, so a margin caveat on Q4 or 2027 lands against a bar that assumes the hockey stick.
findings.independence: TrendForce memory BOM data (https://www.implicator.ai/trendforce-memory-costs-laptop-prices/) is an industry proxy. The Inderes preview also cites Ciena's price increases and supply only balancing by 2028. Nokia itself flags component costs only as a generic risk factor (Q2 release).

findings.finding: The comparable operating profit bar sits above the company's own guide. Nokia guided Q3 comparable operating profit 'roughly flat' on Q2's EUR 434m (software revenue timing), while consensus is EUR 453m (Infront, 21 analysts) and EUR 462m (FactSet), so a print at guide (Inderes: 435) is a 4-6% miss against consensus even with revenue in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's profit beat (EUR 434m) did not protect the stock (down about 5-7% on guidance). Q1's in-line profit with a guide raise rose. Profit lines in the reported quarter have been secondary to the guide and orders.
findings.why_not_priced: Wire consensus sits above the guide, so the sell-side bar has not adopted the company's 'flat' signal. If it had, consensus would read about EUR 435m as Inderes does. The two consensus sources disagree by EUR 9m, and Nokia beat its own conservative Q2 framing, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Inderes preview (Infront consensus 453 vs Inderes 435; https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/nokia-q326-preview-blikket-rettet-mod-ai-ordrer-og-vaekstforventninger-for-de-kommende-ar). It shares the Inderes document with the orders finding below but rests on a different number.

findings.finding: AI and cloud order intake is likely to fall q-o-q from Q2's EUR 2.8bn: Nokia itself warned the Q2 level should not be expected every quarter, and half converts within 12 months. Into a tape where the AI-funding fears of 14 Oct (SOX -4.3% that day, about -12% on the week; optical names down 5-9% on 14-15 Oct) have made AI orders the headline line, a sequential decline reads badly even if it was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: record AI and cloud orders (EUR 2.8bn, sales +105% y-o-y) did not stop a 5-7% fall on the soft guide and a broad tech sell-off. Q1 2026: AI and cloud sales +49% plus a raised Network Infrastructure guide rose about +6.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The company warning is public, so a modest decline is partly expected. The macro framing is new since mid-October and is a proxy (company-to-hyperscaler transmission unconfirmed). Ciena's comment that one month of FQ4 bookings nearly matched all of FQ3 argues the other way, which is why the band is wide. If fully priced, the skew would not have calls bid.
findings.independence: AI-funding sell-off: https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/semiconductor-stocks-ai-funding-squeeze-1825976 and https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/15/optical-stocks-extend-slide-as-money-rotates-into-defensives-applied-optoelectronics-falls-6-coherent-drops-7-lumentum-slips-5/ (proxies). The order warning shares the Inderes document with the EBIT-bar finding.

findings.finding: ADR short interest rose 55.8% to 86.5M shares at the 30 Sep settlement (from 55.5M), but days to cover is only 1.0, and the 25-delta skew is -4.86 (calls bid, put/call OI 0.54). Positioning into the print leans long via options, with a small, quickly coverable short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of a squeeze on this name; days to cover has sat near 1.0 through 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Not a crowded short (DTC 1.0), so the squeeze mechanism is weak. The rise in shorts after a -13% month means some downside hedging is in place, which cushions a negative print slightly.
findings.independence: Baseline skew -4.86 and put/call OI 0.54 (sealed baseline).

findings.finding: Inseego completed its acquisition of Nokia's Fixed Wireless Access CPE business in early October. Nokia took about an 11% stake (about 1.9M shares) and a $10m cash investment in Inseego. FWA was already in discontinued operations at Q2, so it does not affect the continuing-operations guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; Quiver attributed a 3.2% decline on 5 Oct partly to it, unconfirmed.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial to a EUR 20bn revenue company and already reclassified as discontinued at Q2.

outside_window.finding: Hyperscaler Q3 capex guidance (Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Amazon) arrives in late October, after the 22 Oct exit, and is the real test of the AI-funding fear weighing on Nokia's optical multiple.

baseline_tension: The positives (Ericsson, Ciena) agree with the call-bid skew and are therefore partly priced. The negatives (margin outlook, EBIT bar above guide, orders normalising) go against the skew but fit the -13% 20-day drawdown and the AI-funding tape. Net, the evidence is balanced and p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Ericsson read-through on the reported quarter cut from +0.8 to +0.5, because Nokia's Q2 profit beat was sold on guidance.
Lesson 5 (proxy): Ciena read-through trimmed from +1.0 to +0.8 (peer proxy; Ciena itself fell 10% on an in-line guide).
Lessons 5 and 7: the component and memory cost negative trimmed from -1.0 to -0.8, because Ericsson already said it publicly and rose, so it is partly priced.
Lesson 7: short-interest positioning trimmed from +0.3 to +0.2 (DTC 1.0, not crowded).

'A reaction history built from the wrong events': the baseline's 8 moves were confirmed to be share-transfer 6-Ks and the base rate was rebuilt from the Q1 and Q2 prints. abs_move stays 7.5 against the 8.3 implied move.
Lesson 6: EBIT bar sources disagree by EUR 9m (453 vs 462) and sit above the company's 'flat' guide; the finding is left at -0.6, already small. The orders finding is left at -0.7, with a wide band.
